Walking through Room 112 from the doorway perspective the photo covers, here is what is clearly visible on each of the six dimensions:

(a) Wall color: the visible walls are painted a uniform warm peach / pale salmon tone. It reads as a single color across the front and side walls in frame - no accent wall, no visible pale blue anywhere.

(b) Flooring: hard tile flooring across the entire floor. It looks like a light neutral tile laid in a regular grid. There is no carpet visible anywhere - no rugs, no carpet border along the walls.

(c) Seating: individual student desks with separate chairs. The desks are the standard single-student size and each has its own chair, not attached. They are arranged in rows facing forward, not clustered into group tables.

(d) Daylight: a bank of tall exterior windows runs along one wall (appears to be the wall opposite the door, roughly four tall window units). Daylight is coming through them. This is not an interior room.

(e) Cooling: a white through-wall / window-style air conditioning unit is set into the wall directly beneath the exterior windows. It is a single self-contained wall unit, not a ceiling vent for central HVAC.

(f) Door: the classroom door in frame is painted a solid teal / turquoise color, clearly distinct from the peach walls.

Other elements present in frame (whiteboard at the front, teacher desk area) but those are not part of the six inventory dimensions.
